4. For U4 (decouple execution context from job launch): We'll implement the fix in Spring Batch core first, then update XD's Batch module to use the new decoupled context API, removing the XD-2486 workaround code.

6. For U6 (XD-on-Lattice/Diego pluggable SPI): We'll define a generic ModuleDeployment SPI interface that abstracts deployment target specifics, with Receptor as the first implementation, and refactor existing Lattice/Diego code to use the SPI.
7. For U7 (module docs shortDescription): We'll add a mandatory shortDescription field to the module metadata YAML/JSON schema, and update all existing module docs to include this field, plus add validation to fail module upload if shortDescription is missing.
8. For U8 (Python script hosting on HDFS): We'll add a hdfs.script.base.path configuration property to the shell processor, and implement logic to fetch Python scripts from HDFS before execution, with local caching to avoid repeated HDFS reads.

technical_and_design_decisions: For U1 (wiki migration): Store wiki content as Markdown files in a /docs directory within the project repository, using Git for versioning and the repository's native Markdown rendering for wiki display.

For U2 (Hadoop namenode config): Introduce a dedicated spring.hadoop.namenode.address configuration property in XD's default config, with fallback to existing environment variable lookup if the property is unset.
For U3 (jdbchdfs passthrough): Add a passthrough.mode boolean flag to the jdbchdfs batch module that disables chunk processing and uses direct stream read/write when enabled.

For U4 (execution context decoupling): Implement the decoupled execution context fix in Spring Batch core first, then update XD's Batch module to use the new API, removing the existing XD-2486 workaround.

For U5 (Java Config custom job modules): Extend XD's module deployment logic to scan for @Configuration annotated classes in uploaded job JARs, and fix the job existence check to validate full module deployment before allowing launch.

For U6 (pluggable deployment SPI): Define a generic ModuleDeployment SPI that abstracts deployment target operations, with the Receptor API as the first concrete implementation, refactoring existing Lattice/Diego code to use the SPI.

For U7 (module shortDescription): Add a mandatory shortDescription field to the XD module metadata schema, with validation to reject modules missing this field, and update all existing module documentation to include the field.

For U8 (HDFS Python script hosting): Add a hdfs.script.base.path configuration property to the XD shell processor, with logic to fetch Python scripts from HDFS and cache them locally for subsequent runs.
assumptions: The development team has read/write access to all relevant codebases (Spring Batch, Spring XD, Hadoop integration modules) and associated issue trackers.
Existing automated test suites for all affected modules are available and can be executed locally to validate changes without regressions.
The Hadoop namenode address format is consistent across all target deployment environments, so a single configuration property is sufficient for all use cases.
The Receptor API has stable, publicly documented interfaces that can be used to implement the pluggable deployment SPI without breaking changes.
A compatible Python runtime is pre-installed on all target XD-on-Cloud Foundry instances, so no additional runtime provisioning is required for the shell processor functionality.
The target project repository for wiki migration (U1) is already created and accessible to all development team members.
